headline: Three student teachers made The Oregon Trail in 1971. They never saw a dime from it.
slides: Don Rawitsch, Bill Heinemann and Paul Dillenberger were Carleton College seniors, student teaching in Minneapolis.
The first version ran on a teletype: every turn was printed out on a roll of paper.
It debuted in Rawitsch's 8th-grade history class. When the term ended, they shut it down and took the code home.
Rawitsch brought it back at the Minnesota Educational Computing Consortium, which put it in schools across the state.
At its peak, about one in three US school districts had it.
Over 65 million copies sold. The three creators never got a cut.
sources: Sources: Minnesota Historical Society (MNopedia), Carleton College, Fast Company (2021)
